- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.11) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- After sharp price spikes (≥5% from prior period), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +3% above prior peak for next 3–5 periods.
- If sentiment turns negative (≤-0.28) within 5 days, model frequently fails to adjust downward; apply downward bias of 1–2% per negative sentiment unit.
- Mean reversion is strong in 30-day horizon: if forecast is >10% above 30-day moving average, reduce by 1–2% per period until convergence.
- When sentiment is neutral (0.00–0.11), model often underestimates; add 0.5–1.5% to forecast to account for latent momentum.
- Lagged sentiment (e.g., 3–5 day sentiment) better predicts 30-day outcome than current sentiment; weight past sentiment more heavily in correction.
